title: staxtrace.memory/1 agent-output envelope
description: The stable, versioned contract for `stackunderflow memory <cmd> --json`. Every envelope-emitting subcommand (decisions/file/worked/sessions/ask) renders through cli_helpers/agent_output.py into one of two shapes: a success envelope or, on a non-zero exit, an error envelope. This schema freezes the STABLE OUTER envelope only. The per-command `results[]` row internals are deliberately product-shaped and left unconstrained here (see $defs.result_row): they are owned by the discovery layer and evolve independently, so validate rows at the envelope level, not field-by-field. Objects are intentionally open (no additionalProperties:false) so an unknown ADDITIVE field is forward-compatible -- preserved and ignored, never rejected.

schema_tag.description: The frozen contract id. The trailing integer is the MAJOR version and bumps only on a breaking change to the envelope; a consumer pins it and refuses an unknown major.

command.description: Which agent-facing command produced this envelope -- a `memory` subcommand (decisions/file/worked/sessions/ask) or a top-level command that reuses the same envelope (context-replay). Also tags which product-shaped row shape `results[]` carries. This enum is ADDITIVE: a new producer appends a value (existing consumers pinned to the old set still validate every envelope they were built for); it is not a breaking change and does not bump the schema major.

query.description: Command-specific echo of the resolved inputs (e.g. decisions->text, file->path, worked->action, sessions->path+scope, ask->question, plus project/since/limit). Present in both success and error envelopes so a caller can correlate the response with its call. Internals vary by command and are intentionally NOT constrained here.

result_row.description: One product-shaped result row. The envelope's top-level `command` tags which row shape this is (a session match, an outcome match, a file-touch record, ...). Row internals are DELIBERATELY unconstrained at the contract level: they are owned by the discovery layer, are product-shaped (never a 1:1 mirror of SQLite columns), and evolve on their own cadence. Constrain rows here only to `object`.

success_envelope.description: Emitted on exit 0: the token-bounded result envelope an agent splices into its context window.

results.description: The command-specific rows, in the order the discovery layer produced them (rank- or recency-ordered per command). Packed to fit `budget`; `truncated` says whether rows were dropped.

result_count.description: Number of rows in `results` after budget packing (len(results)).

token_estimate.description: chars/4 token estimate of `results` -- what the caller is about to spend.

budget.description: The --context-budget that was enforced (0 means packing was disabled).

truncated.description: True when the budget dropped at least one otherwise-matching row.

risk.description: Documented optional extra, present only for `command:file`: the file-risk summary (revert/fail/work counts + touch total). Its internals are command-owned and not constrained here.

note.description: Documented optional extra, present only for `command:ask`: a human-readable note on which retrieval mode ran (keyword-only vs hybrid).

vector_used.description: Documented optional extra, present only for `command:ask`: whether the semantic vector half of hybrid retrieval ran.

error_envelope.description: Emitted on a non-zero exit: stdout is this error envelope, NOT a result envelope. `schema`/`command`/`query` are retained so a caller can correlate the failure with the call it made.

error.description: Human-readable failure message. Its presence (and the absence of `results`) is what distinguishes an error envelope from a success envelope.
